excitation_report: Full child-vs-parent system comparison on the S trajectory (300 pts, t in [0,120], sigma=1.0 on dS_dt). The NEW superspreading term (-beta*S*I/N_total * alpha_behav*I/(I_half+I)) produces a max target-trajectory effect of ~655*sigma, strongest early at t~10 where prevalence I rises through I_half=50. New mechanism is clearly visible; k=5 threshold passed with large margin. Inherited terms (density-dependent transmission, saturating stock-limited vaccination, waning) were validated upstream and remain active over this window.

alpha_behav: P->P (confirmed, fixed; new-term amplitude, set 1.5 within hint 0-2)
I_half: P->P (confirmed, fixed; set 50 within hint 5-500)
rationale: Typed ode_system contract inherited verbatim: state_variables, state_rhs, initial_conditions, and target RHS are unchanged. Roles are fixed by the contract (S=target/dependent, t=sole time axis, {S,I,V,V_stock}=states, remaining 11 symbols=parameters); integration dummies are absent. Parameters chosen for a physically sensible vaccination-during-outbreak scenario: R0=beta/gamma=2.5, waning ~50-day scale, saturating vaccination logistics (K_half=100, V_cap=50) fed by delivery phi=10 against spoilage delta=0.02. alpha_behav=1.5 and I_half=50 sit inside the suggested hints and make the new superspreading enhancement strongly visible (655*sigma) as prevalence climbs through I_half early in the outbreak. sigma=1.0 on dS_dt is small vs the dominant transmission term (tens) yet serves as the visibility yardstick.

scenario_text: A vaccination campaign moves individuals from the susceptible pool into a protected class while an infection circulates. Modelers examine how the depletion of susceptibles through both natural infection and vaccination determines whether the outbreak is contained. The vaccination rate acts alongside transmission and recovery. Population turnover is negligible over the campaign period.
